A sperm cell's long journey to the egg.Testis: Sperm are made in coiled seminiferous tubules over about 70 days, and the testes hang outside because they need to be cooler than body temperature.
A sperm cell's long journey to the egg.Epididymis: This coiled tube is about six metres long if unraveled, and sperm mature and gain the ability to swim here.
A sperm cell's long journey to the egg.Vas deferens: This is the tube cut in a vasectomy. Muscle contractions push sperm along it during ejaculation.
A sperm cell's long journey to the egg.Ejaculatory duct: Fluid from the seminal vesicles joins sperm here, and that fluid makes up most of semen's volume.
A sperm cell's long journey to the egg.Urethra: It carries both urine and semen, though a valve at the bladder closes during ejaculation so they never mix.
A sperm cell's long journey to the egg.Vagina: The environment is acidic, around pH 4, so sperm hurry into the alkaline mucus of the cervix.
A sperm cell's long journey to the egg.Cervix: Mucus thins around ovulation to let sperm swim through, and it can shelter them for several days.
A sperm cell's long journey to the egg.Uterus: Of the millions that start the journey, only a small fraction reach the fallopian tubes.
A sperm cell's long journey to the egg.Fallopian tube isthmus: The narrow lower tube acts as a reservoir where sperm wait, slowing down until ovulation signals them on.
A sperm cell's long journey to the egg.Ampulla, where the egg waits: Fertilisation usually happens here. The sperm must break through the egg's outer layers using enzymes.

When these Russian rulers came to power.Ivan the Terrible: He was crowned the first tsar of Russia, and the Russian nickname grozny is better translated as formidable.
When these Russian rulers came to power.Michael Romanov: Elected at 16, he ended the Time of Troubles and founded the dynasty that ruled until 1917.
When these Russian rulers came to power.Peter the Great: He founded St Petersburg in 1703, traveled Europe incognito to learn shipbuilding, and once taxed men's beards.
When these Russian rulers came to power.Catherine the Great: A German-born princess who seized power, she greatly expanded the empire and corresponded with Voltaire.
When these Russian rulers came to power.Alexander I: He defeated Napoleon's invasion in 1812 and rode into Paris two years later.
When these Russian rulers came to power.Alexander II: He freed the serfs in 1861 and was assassinated in 1881 by revolutionaries.
When these Russian rulers came to power.Nicholas II: The last tsar abdicated in 1917 and was executed with his family in 1918.
When these Russian rulers came to power.Vladimir Lenin: Leader of the Bolsheviks in the October Revolution, his preserved body lies in a mausoleum on Red Square.
When these Russian rulers came to power.Nikita Khrushchev: He denounced Stalin's crimes in a secret speech in 1956, and faced the Cuban Missile Crisis.
When these Russian rulers came to power.Mikhail Gorbachev: The last leader of the Soviet Union won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1990.

Painters, by birth year.Leonardo da Vinci: Leonardo's Mona Lisa has no visible eyebrows, and he filled notebooks with inventions and anatomy, written in mirror script.
Painters, by birth year.Rembrandt: Rembrandt left close to a hundred self-portraits in paintings, etchings and drawings, a visual autobiography.
Painters, by birth year.Johannes Vermeer: He left only about three dozen paintings and was long forgotten, until Girl with a Pearl Earring made him a household name.
Painters, by birth year.Francisco Goya: Goya went deaf in his 40s, and his dark Black Paintings were painted on the walls of his own house.
Painters, by birth year.J.M.W. Turner: He reportedly had himself lashed to a ship's mast in a snowstorm to experience it before painting Snow Storm.
Painters, by birth year.Claude Monet: The movement Impressionism got its name from his painting Impression, Sunrise, which a critic mocked.
Painters, by birth year.Vincent van Gogh: He sold very few paintings in his lifetime, yet produced over 2,000 works in roughly a decade.
Painters, by birth year.Pablo Picasso: He co-founded Cubism with Georges Braque and made tens of thousands of works in his long career.
Painters, by birth year.Frida Kahlo: She painted around 55 self-portraits, many exploring the pain from a bus accident at age 18.
Painters, by birth year.Andy Warhol: His Campbell's Soup cans and Marilyn prints turned mass-produced goods into art, and his studio was called the Factory.

The Stations of the Cross, in order.Condemned to death: Pilate, the Roman governor, sentenced Jesus to be crucified, and the Roman official's name still appears in the Christian creeds.
The Stations of the Cross, in order.Takes up his cross: In this station Jesus is made to carry the wooden crossbeam, which may have weighed around 30 to 40 kilograms.
The Stations of the Cross, in order.Meets his mother: Tradition has Jesus meet his mother Mary along the way; this scene is not told in the Gospels but is very old in Christian devotion.
The Stations of the Cross, in order.Simon of Cyrene helps: The Gospels name Simon of Cyrene, a passerby from North Africa who was forced to carry the cross, as the father of Alexander and Rufus.
The Stations of the Cross, in order.Veronica wipes his face: Veronica is not named in the Gospels; her cloth, bearing the image of his face, belongs to pious tradition, and her name might mean 'true image'.
The Stations of the Cross, in order.Meets the women of Jerusalem: Jesus tells the weeping women of Jerusalem to weep for themselves and their children, a moment found in the Gospel of Luke.
The Stations of the Cross, in order.Stripped of his garments: Roman crucifixion often involved stripping the victim, and the Gospels note soldiers casting lots for Jesus's seamless tunic.
The Stations of the Cross, in order.Nailed to the cross: Nailing is mentioned in John's Gospel; archaeologists found a first-century heel bone with an iron nail, a rare physical trace of crucifixion.
The Stations of the Cross, in order.Dies on the cross: The 12th station marks the death at Golgotha, and the Gospels note darkness, an earthquake and the temple veil tearing in two.
The Stations of the Cross, in order.Laid in the tomb: Joseph of Arimathea, a wealthy council member, offered his own unused tomb, and the 14th station closes the traditional devotion.

Obscure metric prefixes by size.quecto-: Added in 2022, this is the smallest official prefix, meaning one nonillionth, so tiny that it is almost beyond any measurement.
Obscure metric prefixes by size.yocto-: The prefix comes from octo, because it is 1000 raised to the eighth power, a pattern many of the biggest and smallest prefixes follow.
Obscure metric prefixes by size.atto-: This one comes from the Danish word atten, meaning eighteen, since it is 1000 to the power of minus six, or ten to the minus eighteen.
Obscure metric prefixes by size.femto-: The name comes from the Danish femten, fifteen, and femtosecond lasers are so fast they are used in eye surgery.
Obscure metric prefixes by size.deca-: It is rarely used, but in central Europe cheese and ham are still sold by the dekagram, which equals ten grams.
Obscure metric prefixes by size.hecto-: Hectares and weather forecasters' hectopascals both use it, and it simply means a hundred, from Greek hekaton.
Obscure metric prefixes by size.peta-: The name comes from the Greek penta, for five, because it is 1000 to the fifth power, and a petabyte is a thousand terabytes.
Obscure metric prefixes by size.exa-: The name comes from hexa, six, being 1000 to the sixth power, and an exabyte is roughly all of the words humans have ever spoken, by some estimates.
Obscure metric prefixes by size.zetta-: Global data creation is now measured in zettabytes, and the prefix was added to the metric system in 1991.
Obscure metric prefixes by size.quetta-: Added in 2022 as the largest prefix, it lets us say that Jupiter weighs about 1.9 quettagrams, a handy way to talk about planets.

From the Big Bang to the Moon landing.The Big Bang: Not an explosion in space but the expansion of space itself, whose faint afterglow, the cosmic microwave background, still reaches us.
From the Big Bang to the Moon landing.The Sun forms: The Sun formed from a collapsing gas cloud, and holds about 99.8 percent of all the mass in the solar system.
From the Big Bang to the Moon landing.The Moon forms: Most scientists think it formed when a Mars-sized body, called Theia, slammed into the young Earth.
From the Big Bang to the Moon landing.Earliest life on Earth: Evidence comes from chemical traces and layered stromatolites in Greenland and Western Australia, and some of it is still debated.
From the Big Bang to the Moon landing.Great Oxidation Event: Oxygen released by cyanobacteria flooded the air, killing many anaerobic microbes and rusting iron out of the oceans.
From the Big Bang to the Moon landing.Cambrian explosion: Hard shells and complex body plans arose in a fairly short span, and the Burgess Shale in Canada preserves some stunning fossils.
From the Big Bang to the Moon landing.First dinosaurs: Small, two-legged early dinosaurs such as Eoraptor, found in Argentina, were hardly the giants that came later.
From the Big Bang to the Moon landing.Dinosaur-killing asteroid: A rock about 10 kilometres wide hit near Chicxulub in Mexico, leaving a worldwide layer of iridium-rich clay as evidence.
From the Big Bang to the Moon landing.Homo sapiens appears: The oldest fossils that belong to our species, from Jebel Irhoud in Morocco, are about 300,000 years old.
From the Big Bang to the Moon landing.Apollo 11 lands: On a one-year calendar of Earth's history, this human milestone happened in a fraction of the final second.

Chinese zodiac animals of the coming lun.Rat: In legend the Rat won the Jade Emperor's race by riding the Ox's back and jumping ahead at the finish.
Chinese zodiac animals of the coming lun.Ox: A symbol of diligence, in the myth it carried the Rat across the river in the race.
Chinese zodiac animals of the coming lun.Tiger: Tradition says the stripes on a tiger's forehead resemble the character for king, and the animal stands for courage.
Chinese zodiac animals of the coming lun.Rabbit: In the Vietnamese zodiac the Cat replaces it.
Chinese zodiac animals of the coming lun.Dragon: It is the only mythical creature in the zodiac, and in Chinese tradition it is benevolent, linked to rain and emperors.
Chinese zodiac animals of the coming lun.Snake: In Chinese myth, the creator goddess Nüwa is depicted with a snake's body, and the animal is linked to wisdom.
Chinese zodiac animals of the coming lun.Horse: It corresponds to the hours 11 am to 1 pm, which is why noon in Chinese, zhongwu, means middle of the horse hour.
Chinese zodiac animals of the coming lun.Goat: The Chinese word yang covers goat, sheep and ram, so translations of this sign vary.
Chinese zodiac animals of the coming lun.Monkey: The trickster Sun Wukong, in the novel Journey to the West, is the best known literary monkey.
Chinese zodiac animals of the coming lun.Rooster: It is the only bird of the twelve zodiac animals, and its hour is five to seven in the evening.

Firsts in written messages.First printed newspaper: Johann Carolus's weekly Relation, printed in Strasbourg, is usually credited as the first true newspaper. Before it, news spread by handwritten sheets.
Firsts in written messages.Penny Black postage stamp: The world's first adhesive postage stamp showed Queen Victoria's profile. It cost one penny and made the sender, not the recipient, pay.
Firsts in written messages.\"What hath God wrought\": Samuel Morse sent these words from Washington to Baltimore, a phrase from the Bible's Book of Numbers. It launched the commercial telegraph era.
Firsts in written messages.First transatlantic telegram: The cable between Ireland and Newfoundland carried Queen Victoria's greeting to President Buchanan, but it failed within weeks and a durable link came in 1866.
Firsts in written messages.First postcard: The Austro-Hungarian "Correspondenz-Karte" went on sale in Vienna in 1869. Its open message cost less to send than a sealed letter.
Firsts in written messages.First email: Ray Tomlinson sent it between two computers in the same room and chose the @ sign to separate user from machine name.
Firsts in written messages.First :-) emoticon: Scott Fahlman proposed it on a university message board to mark jokes, and he suggested the sideways sign for the solemn one too.
Firsts in written messages.First text message (SMS): Neil Papworth sent "Merry Christmas" to a Vodafone colleague's phone in the UK. It would be years before texting became common.
Firsts in written messages.First emoji set: Shigetaka Kurita designed 176 tiny 12-by-12 pixel pictures for Japan's NTT DoCoMo i-mode phones. Some are now in the Museum of Modern Art.
Firsts in written messages.First tweet: Jack Dorsey posted "just setting up my twttr" in March, a reminder that the service's early name dropped its vowels.

Generations from Adam to Noah.Adam: The first man in the Book of Genesis, created in God's image, according to the Bible, and said to have lived 930 years.
Generations from Adam to Noah.Seth: The third son of Adam and Eve, born after Abel's death, and the ancestor of Noah. Genesis says he lived 912 years.
Generations from Adam to Noah.Enosh: Seth's son, whose name means "mortal" or "man". Genesis says that at this time people "began to call upon the name of the Lord".
Generations from Adam to Noah.Kenan: Genesis gives him 910 years. His name is thought to mean "possession" or "smith" in Hebrew, but the Bible says little else about him.
Generations from Adam to Noah.Mahalalel: Genesis says he lived 895 years, and his name means "praise of God" in Hebrew.
Generations from Adam to Noah.Jared: His name means "descent" in Hebrew, and in Genesis he is the father of Enoch, and lived 962 years.
Generations from Adam to Noah.Enoch: Genesis says he "walked with God" and was taken at only 365 years, short by his family's standards. A later Book of Enoch is attributed to him.
Generations from Adam to Noah.Methuselah: The oldest person in the Bible, at 969 years. His name has become a byword for extreme age.
Generations from Adam to Noah.Lamech: Father of Noah, who said that Noah would bring comfort from the ground that God had cursed, according to Genesis. He lived 777 years.
Generations from Adam to Noah.Noah: Built an ark to survive the flood, and took two of every animal, according to the Bible, and his three sons populated the world afterwards.

When these leagues kicked off.MLB's National League: Baseball's oldest major league, founded in 1876, still has the Chicago Cubs and Atlanta Braves franchises.
When these leagues kicked off.English Football League: The world's first professional football league began with 12 clubs, mostly from the English Midlands and North.
When these leagues kicked off.Victorian Football League: This Australian-rules competition began with a handful of Melbourne clubs and later became the AFL.
When these leagues kicked off.NHL: Founded in Montreal, this league began with just a few teams, and its championship trophy is the Stanley Cup.
When these leagues kicked off.NFL (as the APFA): The American Professional Football Association was formed in a car showroom in Canton, Ohio, and soon renamed itself.
When these leagues kicked off.La Liga: Spain's top division began in 1929, and Barcelona and Real Madrid have dominated it ever since.
When these leagues kicked off.BAA (today's NBA): Merged with a rival in 1949 to become the NBA, the Basketball Association of America began in 1946.
When these leagues kicked off.Bundesliga: Germany's top flight began after decades of regional leagues, and it is known for low ticket prices and packed stands.
When these leagues kicked off.Premier League: England's top clubs broke away from the Football League in 1992 to negotiate their own TV deals.
When these leagues kicked off.Indian Premier League: This cricket league mixed the sport with Bollywood-style glamour, and it's now among the richest in the world per match.

When these opera houses and concert hall.La Scala, Milan: It opened with Salieri's opera and stands on the site of a church, Santa Maria alla Scala, which gave the house its name.
When these opera houses and concert hall.La Fenice, Venice: Its name means 'the phoenix', fitting for a theatre that burned down in 1836 and again in a 1996 arson fire, then rose again.
When these opera houses and concert hall.Royal Opera House (current): Covent Garden's present house is the third theatre on its site; the earlier two were destroyed by fire.
When these opera houses and concert hall.Vienna State Opera: Bombed in 1945, it was rebuilt and reopened in 1955, and it hosts the glittering Vienna Opera Ball each year.
When these opera houses and concert hall.Palais Garnier, Paris: The setting for The Phantom of the Opera; beneath it lies a real underground cistern that inspired the legend of a lake.
When these opera houses and concert hall.Teatro Colón, Buenos Aires: Famed for its acoustics, this horseshoe-shaped house in Argentina is ranked among the world's best for opera.
When these opera houses and concert hall.The Met at Lincoln Center: It replaced the old Met on Broadway, opening with Samuel Barber's Antony and Cleopatra and Chagall murals in the lobby.
When these opera houses and concert hall.Sydney Opera House: Danish architect Jorn Utzon's sail-like design won a competition, but he left the project before it was done; it is now UNESCO listed.
When these opera houses and concert hall.Oslo Opera House: Its marble roof slopes down to the harbour so that visitors can walk up onto it, a rare feature among opera houses.
When these opera houses and concert hall.Elbphilharmonie, Hamburg: Built on top of an old brick warehouse, this glass concert hall arrived years late and far over budget, but became a landmark.

When these newspapers were founded.The Times (London): It began in 1785 as the Daily Universal Register and took the name The Times in 1788. Its nickname was 'The Thunderer'.
When these newspapers were founded.The Guardian: Founded as the Manchester Guardian, it moved to London and dropped 'Manchester' from its name in 1959. A famous spelling slip earned it the nickname 'Grauniad'.
When these newspapers were founded.Le Figaro: It is named for the barber in Beaumarchais's plays, and is France's oldest national daily still in print.
When these newspapers were founded.The New York Times: Its motto 'All the News That's Fit to Print' dates from 1896, when Adolph Ochs bought the struggling paper and rebuilt it.
When these newspapers were founded.The Washington Post: Its reporting on the Watergate break-in, led by Woodward and Bernstein, helped bring down President Nixon in 1974.
When these newspapers were founded.The Wall Street Journal: Charles Dow's company launched it, and Dow also created the Dow Jones Industrial Average, still a headline number.
When these newspapers were founded.Daily Mail: It was a halfpenny paper aimed at a new mass readership, and was among the first in Britain to sell a million copies a day.
When these newspapers were founded.Pravda: Its name means 'truth' in Russian. It was the Communist Party's official paper for most of the Soviet era.
When these newspapers were founded.Le Monde: It launched after France's liberation from Nazi occupation, at de Gaulle's request, to replace the discredited wartime press.
When these newspapers were founded.USA Today: It was the first national general-interest daily in the US, and its colourful graphics and weather maps were widely copied.

Grocery chains, by founding year.A&P: The Great Atlantic and Pacific Tea Company once sold tea by mail, and it grew into a nationwide chain that was the biggest retailer in the U.S. for decades.
Grocery chains, by founding year.Kroger: Barney Kroger opened his first store in Cincinnati, and the chain became the largest traditional supermarket company in the country.
Grocery chains, by founding year.Safeway: Its name was meant to signal safety, and its founder, Marion Skaggs, built it from a small store in Idaho into one of the largest chains in the U.S.
Grocery chains, by founding year.Woolworths (Australia): The Australian giant has no connection with the American Woolworths dime store; the name was borrowed in Sydney by a store founder in 1924.
Grocery chains, by founding year.Publix: Founder George Jenkins' stores are famous for their 'Where shopping is a pleasure' slogan, and the chain is owned by its employees.
Grocery chains, by founding year.Carrefour: This French retailer is credited with inventing the hypermarket, a huge supermarket and department store in one, in 1963.
Grocery chains, by founding year.Trader Joe's: The chain began as a Southern California store, and it is known for private-label products and for its cheerful Hawaiian-style staff shirts.
Grocery chains, by founding year.Lidl (first store): The German discounter opened its first store in 1973, and it is known for its low prices and weekly special offers.
Grocery chains, by founding year.Whole Foods Market: Founded in Austin, Texas, it popularised natural and organic foods before being bought by Amazon for 13.7 billion dollars.
Grocery chains, by founding year.AmazonFresh: Launched in Seattle, it was an online grocery delivery service that ran as a pilot years before Amazon bought a physical grocery chain.

How many bones are in it?.Middle ear: The stapes in the middle ear is the smallest bone in the body, about three millimeters long.
How many bones are in it?.Ankle (tarsals): The seven tarsal bones include the calcaneus, the heel bone, the largest bone in the foot.
How many bones are in it?.Wrist (carpals): Of the eight wrist bones, the scaphoid is the one most often broken, usually after a fall on an outstretched hand.
How many bones are in it?.Fingers of one hand: Each finger has three bones but the thumb only two, giving 14 finger bones called phalanges in a hand.
How many bones are in it?.Skull: The skull has 8 cranial and 14 facial bones, and the jaw is the only one that can move, which is why it can hinge for chewing.
How many bones are in it?.Rib cage (ribs only): There are twelve pairs of ribs, and the lowest two pairs, called floating ribs, are not attached at the front.
How many bones are in it?.One foot: The two feet hold 52 of the body's 206 bones, about a quarter of the skeleton, so each foot has 26.
How many bones are in it?.One hand: Your two hands hold 54 bones, over a quarter of the skeleton's 206, which gives them their fine dexterity.
How many bones are in it?.Adult skeleton: The femur, or thigh bone, is the longest and strongest in the body, and can support many times your weight.
How many bones are in it?.Newborn skeleton: Many of a newborn's bones will fuse as it grows, and soft spots in the skull let the head squeeze through birth.

Marine mammals by weight.Sea otter: Its fur is the densest of any animal, around a million hairs per square inch, since otters lack blubber.
Marine mammals by weight.Harbor porpoise: Among the smallest cetaceans, this shy porpoise rarely leaps like dolphins and often avoids boats.
Marine mammals by weight.Harbor seal: Pups can swim within hours of birth, which helps them survive on tidal sandbanks.
Marine mammals by weight.Bottlenose dolphin: Each dolphin develops a signature whistle that works like a name, and others use it to call them.
Marine mammals by weight.West Indian manatee: Its closest living relatives are elephants, a sign that sea cows evolved from land mammals.
Marine mammals by weight.Walrus (male): Both sexes grow tusks, and the genus name Odobenus means 'tooth-walker', for how they haul out onto ice.
Marine mammals by weight.Southern elephant seal (male): The largest seal, it can dive over 2,000 m and hold its breath for as long as two hours.
Marine mammals by weight.Orca (male): The largest dolphin, it lives in matrilineal pods with distinct dialects and hunting cultures.
Marine mammals by weight.Sperm whale (male): It has the biggest brain of any animal, weighing about 8 kg, and dives deep to hunt giant squid.
Marine mammals by weight.Blue whale: The largest animal known to have ever lived, its low calls can carry for hundreds of kilometres underwater.

When these royals and rulers were execut.Atahualpa: The last free Inca emperor was garroted by Pizarro's men after converting to Christianity, which spared him from being burned.
When these royals and rulers were execut.Anne Boleyn: Henry VIII brought in a skilled French swordsman from Calais to behead her, rather than using the usual axe.
When these royals and rulers were execut.Lady Jane Grey: The 'Nine Days' Queen' was a teenager, about 16 or 17, when she was beheaded.
When these royals and rulers were execut.Mary, Queen of Scots: Held captive by Elizabeth I for nearly 19 years, she was executed after a plot against the queen.
When these royals and rulers were execut.Charles I of England: He wore two shirts to the scaffold so he would not shiver and appear afraid.
When these royals and rulers were execut.Louis XVI: He went to the guillotine, a device introduced partly as a more humane way to execute.
When these royals and rulers were execut.Emperor Maximilian of Mexico: Installed as emperor of Mexico by Napoleon III, the Austrian archduke was shot by firing squad at Querétaro.
When these royals and rulers were execut.Nicholas II: Russia's last tsar was shot with his family by Bolsheviks in Yekaterinburg, and DNA later identified the remains.
When these royals and rulers were execut.Nicolae Ceaușescu: He was tried hastily and shot on Christmas Day during the Romanian Revolution.
When these royals and rulers were execut.Saddam Hussein: He was hanged in December 2006 after an Iraqi court convicted him over killings at Dujail.

When these arcade games hit the arcades.Computer Space: Inspired by the university game Spacewar!, it was the first commercial arcade video game, but its controls baffled players.
When these arcade games hit the arcades.Breakout: Atari's brick-smasher was prototyped by Steve Wozniak, who was famously asked to use as few chips as possible.
When these arcade games hit the arcades.Asteroids: Atari's best-selling arcade game let players enter their initials on a high-score table, one of the first games to offer that.
When these arcade games hit the arcades.Galaga: Namco's shooter let enemies swoop out of formation, and a captured ship could be rescued to give you a double fighter.
When these arcade games hit the arcades.Dragon's Lair: Don Bluth's laserdisc game used hand-drawn cartoon animation, which looked like a film, but cost players quarters fast.
When these arcade games hit the arcades.Gauntlet: A four-player dungeon crawler where a voice announced that 'Elf needs food badly', it let friends play together.
When these arcade games hit the arcades.Street Fighter II: It popularized the combo and a roster of fighters, and sparked a rise of fighting game tournaments around the world.
When these arcade games hit the arcades.Tekken: Namco's 3D fighter introduced the Mishima family saga, and became one of the best-selling arcade-turned-home franchises.
When these arcade games hit the arcades.Time Crisis: Players used a light gun and a foot pedal to duck behind cover, giving a real-time shooter a new twist.
When these arcade games hit the arcades.Dance Dance Revolution: Konami's dance machine had players stepping on arrows to the beat, and it made workout-gaming a worldwide fad.

Famous telescopes, by first light or lau.Galileo's telescope: Galileo built it from a lead tube and two lenses, then spotted Jupiter's four big moons, proving not everything circles the Earth.
Famous telescopes, by first light or lau.Newton's reflector: Newton used a curved mirror instead of a lens, dodging the color fringes of refractors; big telescopes still use the idea.
Famous telescopes, by first light or lau.Herschel's 40-foot telescope: Its 1.2-metre mirror and 12-metre tube dwarfed everything before it, and it found two new moons of Saturn, but it was clumsy to use.
Famous telescopes, by first light or lau.Leviathan of Parsonstown: Built in Ireland by the Earl of Rosse, it was the world's largest telescope for decades and first revealed the spiral shape of the Whirlpool Galaxy.
Famous telescopes, by first light or lau.Yerkes refractor: Its 40-inch lens is still the largest refractor used for research; bigger lenses sag under their own weight and blur the view.
Famous telescopes, by first light or lau.Hooker 100-inch telescope: At Mount Wilson, it let Edwin Hubble show that Andromeda is a separate galaxy, hugely enlarging the known universe.
Famous telescopes, by first light or lau.Hale 200-inch telescope: Palomar's giant mirror was the biggest working telescope for about 30 years; its Pyrex glass blank was chosen to resist temperature swings.
Famous telescopes, by first light or lau.Hubble Space Telescope: Launched with a flawed mirror that astronauts fixed in 1993, it has orbited Earth for over three decades sending back sharp images.
Famous telescopes, by first light or lau.Keck I: Its 10-metre mirror is made of 36 hexagonal segments, adjusted constantly, on top of Hawaii's Mauna Kea volcano.
Famous telescopes, by first light or lau.James Webb Space Telescope: It watches in infrared from a point about 1.5 million km from Earth, shielded by a tennis-court-sized sunshade, seeing some of the earliest galaxies.

When these scales and units were devised.Fahrenheit scale: Daniel Fahrenheit made the first reliable mercury thermometers; water freezes at 32 and boils at 212 degrees on his scale.
When these scales and units were devised.Celsius scale: Anders Celsius originally set boiling at 0 and freezing at 100; the scale was flipped after his death.
When these scales and units were devised.Metric system (France): Revolutionary France defined the metre from the Earth's meridian, replacing a messy patchwork of local measures.
When these scales and units were devised.Beaufort wind scale: Admiral Francis Beaufort rated wind from 0 (calm) to 12 (hurricane force) by watching its effect on a sailing ship.
When these scales and units were devised.Mohs hardness scale: Friedrich Mohs ranked minerals by which ones can scratch which, from talc at 1 to diamond at 10.
When these scales and units were devised.Kelvin scale: Lord Kelvin's scale starts at absolute zero, about minus 273 degrees Celsius, where particle motion nearly stops.
When these scales and units were devised.pH scale: Danish chemist Søren Sørensen devised it at the Carlsberg brewery lab; each step is a tenfold change in acidity.
When these scales and units were devised.Scoville heat scale: Wilbur Scoville had tasters sip diluted chili extract until the burn vanished; pure capsaicin sits at around 16 million.
When these scales and units were devised.Richter scale: Created for California quakes, each whole number step means about 32 times more energy released.
When these scales and units were devised.Saffir-Simpson scale: It rates hurricanes from category 1 to 5 by wind speed, and category 5 begins at 157 mph (252 km/h).

How many countries share a land border w.Portugal: Its only land border, with Spain, has barely changed since the 1297 Treaty of Alcañices, one of the oldest in Europe.
How many countries share a land border w.Mongolia: A landlocked country squeezed between Russia and China, it has no direct access to any ocean.
How many countries share a land border w.Mexico: It borders the United States to the north, and Guatemala and Belize to the south.
How many countries share a land border w.Thailand: Myanmar, Laos, Cambodia and Malaysia share its borders, and it is the only Southeast Asian nation never colonized by Europeans.
How many countries share a land border w.Kenya: Its five neighbors are Uganda, Tanzania, Somalia, Ethiopia and South Sudan, and the equator crosses the country.
How many countries share a land border w.Hungary: Landlocked in Central Europe, it touches seven countries, and the Danube bends through it.
How many countries share a land border w.Austria: The Alpine republic shares borders with eight countries, including Germany, Italy and Switzerland.
How many countries share a land border w.Germany: With nine neighbors it touches more countries than any other EU state, from Denmark in the north to Switzerland in the south.
How many countries share a land border w.Brazil: It touches every South American country except Chile and Ecuador.
How many countries share a land border w.China: It shares borders with 14 countries, a number matched only by Russia, from India to North Korea.

Famous science quotes, by when they were.Eureka!: Archimedes supposedly shouted it from his bath on spotting how displaced water could test a crown for gold; the tale comes from Vitruvius, written long after.
Famous science quotes, by when they were.And yet it moves: Galileo is said to have muttered it after being forced to recant, but there is no evidence he did; the line first appears over a century later.
Famous science quotes, by when they were.Shoulders of giants: Newton wrote it in a letter to Robert Hooke, though the image of standing on giants' shoulders was already centuries old.
Famous science quotes, by when they were.What hath God wrought: Samuel Morse's first public telegram quoted the Book of Numbers, a line picked by the daughter of the US patent commissioner.
Famous science quotes, by when they were.Survival of the fittest: Herbert Spencer coined it after reading Darwin, and Darwin adopted the phrase in later editions of On the Origin of Species.
Famous science quotes, by when they were.Mr. Watson, come here: Bell spoke these words to his assistant Thomas Watson in the next room during the first successful telephone transmission.
Famous science quotes, by when they were.E equals mc squared: His 1905 paper showed that mass and energy are interchangeable, and because c squared is huge, a tiny mass holds vast energy.
Famous science quotes, by when they were.God does not play dice: Einstein wrote it to Max Born to object to quantum randomness; Niels Bohr reportedly replied that he should stop telling God what to do.
Famous science quotes, by when they were.The two cultures: C. P. Snow's lecture argued that scientists and literary intellectuals had stopped understanding one another, a split he found dangerous.
Famous science quotes, by when they were.One small step for man: Armstrong said he meant 'one small step for a man', but the 'a' was lost in transmission, or he simply didn't say it.

Golden Age Hollywood stars by birth year.Charlie Chaplin: Born into poverty in London, he created the Tramp and in 1919 co-founded United Artists to control his own films.
Golden Age Hollywood stars by birth year.Humphrey Bogart: He won his only Oscar for The African Queen, and his lisp and scarred lip, from an injury, became part of his tough-guy image.
Golden Age Hollywood stars by birth year.Cary Grant: Born Archibald Leach in Bristol, he is credited with the line 'Everybody wants to be Cary Grant. Even I want to be Cary Grant.'
Golden Age Hollywood stars by birth year.John Wayne: Born Marion Morrison, he got his nickname Duke from the family dog he followed as a boy.
Golden Age Hollywood stars by birth year.Bette Davis: She became the first performer to earn ten Oscar nominations for acting, winning for Dangerous and Jezebel.
Golden Age Hollywood stars by birth year.Judy Garland: She was only 16 when she played Dorothy in The Wizard of Oz, which brought her a special Juvenile Oscar.
Golden Age Hollywood stars by birth year.Marilyn Monroe: Born Norma Jeane Mortenson, she became one of the most photographed people ever, and her name still sells prints and posters.
Golden Age Hollywood stars by birth year.Audrey Hepburn: Born in Brussels, she won an Oscar for Roman Holiday and later devoted herself to UNICEF as a goodwill ambassador.
Golden Age Hollywood stars by birth year.James Dean: He made only three major films, was nominated for two Oscars after his death, and died at 24 in a 1955 car crash.
Golden Age Hollywood stars by birth year.Elizabeth Taylor: A child star in National Velvet, she later became the first actor to be paid a million dollars for one film, Cleopatra.

Early cinema milestones.Roundhay Garden Scene: Louis Le Prince filmed it in Leeds; it's the oldest surviving film, lasting only about two seconds.
Early cinema milestones.Workers Leaving the Factory: The Lumiere brothers shot it in 1895, and its Paris screening in December launched commercial cinema.
Early cinema milestones.A Trip to the Moon: Georges Melies's rocket landing in the Moon's eye is among film's most famous images.
Early cinema milestones.The Great Train Robbery: Edwin S. Porter's early Western ends with a bandit firing straight at the camera.
Early cinema milestones.The Birth of a Nation: D.W. Griffith's epic was technically groundbreaking but notoriously racist, glorifying the Ku Klux Klan.
Early cinema milestones.The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari: A German expressionist horror film with painted, distorted sets and a twist ending.
Early cinema milestones.Nosferatu: An unauthorized Dracula adaptation; Bram Stoker's widow sued and a court ordered all copies destroyed, but some survived.
Early cinema milestones.The Jazz Singer: The first feature with synchronized dialogue, when Al Jolson told the audience, You ain't heard nothin' yet.
Early cinema milestones.City Lights: Chaplin made it years after talkies arrived, and its final scene is often called the most touching in cinema.
Early cinema milestones.King Kong: Willis O'Brien's stop-motion effects brought to life a model ape only about 18 inches tall.

Chess world champions, by first title.Wilhelm Steinitz: The Austrian became the first official champion by beating Zukertort, and developed positional chess.
Chess world champions, by first title.Emanuel Lasker: He held the title for 27 years, the longest reign ever, and was also a mathematician.
Chess world champions, by first title.Jose Raul Capablanca: The Cuban prodigy was known for effortless endgames and went unbeaten for about eight years.
Chess world champions, by first title.Alexander Alekhine: The only champion to die holding the title, in 1946, having lost it to Euwe and won it back.
Chess world champions, by first title.Max Euwe: A Dutch mathematician who later became president of FIDE, chess's governing body.
Chess world champions, by first title.Mikhail Botvinnik: A Soviet electrical engineer who mentored later champions Karpov and Kasparov.
Chess world champions, by first title.Mikhail Tal: The Magician from Riga was the youngest champion at the time, known for sacrificial attacks.
Chess world champions, by first title.Boris Spassky: He beat Petrosian in 1969, then lost the Match of the Century to Fischer.
Chess world champions, by first title.Bobby Fischer: His 1972 win in Reykjavik ended 24 years of Soviet dominance, and he forfeited the title in 1975.
Chess world champions, by first title.Garry Kasparov: The youngest undisputed champion at 22, he lost a match to IBM's Deep Blue in 1997.

When these British PMs first took office.Robert Walpole: He is generally counted as the first Prime Minister, and he was the first to live at 10 Downing Street.
When these British PMs first took office.William Pitt the Younger: He took office at only 24, still the youngest British Prime Minister ever.
When these British PMs first took office.Robert Peel: He founded the Metropolitan Police, whose officers were nicknamed 'bobbies' and 'peelers' after him.
When these British PMs first took office.Benjamin Disraeli: A novelist as well as a statesman, he made Queen Victoria Empress of India.
When these British PMs first took office.David Lloyd George: A native Welsh speaker, he led the country during the final years of the First World War.
When these British PMs first took office.Winston Churchill: He won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1953, and painted as a hobby.
When these British PMs first took office.Clement Attlee: His government created the NHS and took major industries into public ownership.
When these British PMs first took office.Margaret Thatcher: A trained research chemist before politics, she became Britain's first woman Prime Minister.
When these British PMs first took office.Tony Blair: At 43 he was the youngest Prime Minister since 1812, and he led Labour to a landslide.
When these British PMs first took office.Gordon Brown: He had been Chancellor of the Exchequer for ten years before moving into Number 10, and was a son of the manse.

Elevation of these ancient sites.Jericho: Jericho lies near the Dead Sea, far below sea level, and it is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities on Earth.
Elevation of these ancient sites.Alexandria: Alexandria was founded by Alexander the Great in 331 BC on the Mediterranean coast, and it was home to a famed lighthouse and library.
Elevation of these ancient sites.Acropolis of Athens: The Acropolis rises on a rocky hill above Athens, and it's crowned by the Parthenon, a temple for the goddess Athena.
Elevation of these ancient sites.Delphi: Delphi, on the slopes of Mount Parnassus, was home to the Oracle, and the ancient Greeks regarded it as the center of the world.
Elevation of these ancient sites.Old City of Jerusalem: Jerusalem's Old City sits among hills, and it's sacred to Judaism, Christianity and Islam.
Elevation of these ancient sites.Persepolis: Persepolis was the ceremonial capital of the Persian Empire, built on a terrace in the highlands of Iran.
Elevation of these ancient sites.Monte Albán: Monte Albán was a Zapotec capital built on a leveled mountaintop in Oaxaca, Mexico, overlooking three valleys.
Elevation of these ancient sites.Machu Picchu: Machu Picchu was built by the Inca in the 1400s on a mountain ridge, and it was little known outside the region until 1911.
Elevation of these ancient sites.Cusco: Cusco was the capital of the Inca Empire, and its streets still have Inca stonework so precise that mortar wasn't needed.
Elevation of these ancient sites.Tiwanaku: Tiwanaku, near Lake Titicaca in Bolivia, was a major pre-Inca city at one of the highest elevations for any ancient civilization.

Asteroids by mean diameter.Dimorphos: Dimorphos is the moon of asteroid Didymos, and NASA's DART spacecraft hit it in 2022 to test deflecting asteroids.
Asteroids by mean diameter.Itokawa: Itokawa was visited by Japan's Hayabusa, and it brought back the first samples from an asteroid, and it's shaped like a sea otter.
Asteroids by mean diameter.Bennu: Bennu was sampled by NASA's OSIRIS-REx, and it's a rubble pile that carried carbon and water-bearing minerals.
Asteroids by mean diameter.Ryugu: Ryugu was visited by Hayabusa2, and its samples include organic molecules, and it's shaped like a spinning top.
Asteroids by mean diameter.Eros: Eros was the first asteroid orbited by a spacecraft, and it's potato-shaped and about 34 km long.
Asteroids by mean diameter.Ida: Ida has its own tiny moon, Dactyl, and it was the first asteroid found to have a moon.
Asteroids by mean diameter.Psyche: Psyche is likely rich in metal, and NASA launched a probe to it in 2023.
Asteroids by mean diameter.Hygiea: Hygiea is the fourth largest asteroid and may be nearly round, so it could be reclassified as a dwarf planet.
Asteroids by mean diameter.Vesta: Vesta is the second most massive asteroid, and meteorites found on Earth are known to come from it.
Asteroids by mean diameter.Ceres: Ceres is a dwarf planet, and the largest object in the asteroid belt, and it holds about a third of the belt's mass.

Blood's lap around the body.Left ventricle: The left ventricle has the thickest muscle wall in the heart, because it must push blood to your entire body. Its beat is the one you feel at your chest.
Blood's lap around the body.Aortic valve: This valve has three flaps that snap shut after every beat, preventing blood from falling back. It opens roughly 100,000 times a day.
Blood's lap around the body.Aorta: Your largest artery is about as wide as a garden hose. Elastic walls stretch with each pulse and recoil to keep blood moving.
Blood's lap around the body.Artery: Arteries carry blood away from the heart, and their muscular walls are thicker than veins. The pulse you feel at your wrist is one of them.
Blood's lap around the body.Arteriole: These tiny branches act like taps. When they widen or narrow, they control how much blood reaches each organ, and they help set blood pressure.
Blood's lap around the body.Capillary: Some are so narrow that red cells squeeze through in single file. All gas and nutrient exchange happens here, and the body has tens of thousands of kilometres of them.
Blood's lap around the body.Venule: These small vessels gather blood leaving the capillaries and merge into veins. They are also where white blood cells often leave the bloodstream to fight infection.
Blood's lap around the body.Vein: Veins have one-way valves that stop blood sinking back down your legs. At any moment they hold about two-thirds of your blood.
Blood's lap around the body.Vena cava: The two largest veins, superior and inferior, return all of the body's used blood to the heart. The inferior one runs up beside your spine.
Blood's lap around the body.Right atrium: This chamber holds the sinoatrial node, the heart's natural pacemaker. It fires electrical signals that start each heartbeat.

When these Christmas songs came out.Silent Night: First performed in an Austrian church in 1818, reportedly on guitar because the organ was broken.
When these Christmas songs came out.Jingle Bells: James Lord Pierpont wrote it as 'One Horse Open Sleigh', and it may have been written for Thanksgiving.
When these Christmas songs came out.White Christmas (Crosby): Irving Berlin's song is the best-selling single of all time, according to Guinness.
When these Christmas songs came out.Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer: Gene Autry's 1949 recording made it famous; Robert May invented Rudolph for Montgomery Ward in 1939.
When these Christmas songs came out.Jingle Bell Rock: Bobby Helms sang this rock-and-roll Christmas hit, which found new fans in Mean Girls.
When these Christmas songs came out.Feliz Navidad: José Feliciano's song is simple and bilingual, with one Spanish line and one English line.
When these Christmas songs came out.Last Christmas (Wham!): George Michael played every instrument himself, and it was stuck at number two in 1984 before finally topping the UK chart in 2023.
When these Christmas songs came out.All I Want for Christmas: Mariah Carey's song only reached US number one in 2019, 25 years after its release.
When these Christmas songs came out.Mistletoe (Justin Bieber): This single came from Under the Mistletoe, Bieber's Christmas album that topped the US chart.
When these Christmas songs came out.Santa Tell Me (Ariana Grande): A perennial entry on holiday playlists that charts again every season.

How high these are off the floor.Wall power outlet: In accessible design, outlets must sit at least about 38 cm up, so wheelchair users don't have to bend.
How high these are off the floor.Dining chair seat: At around 18 inches, it's meant to let most adults rest their feet flat.
How high these are off the floor.Desk top: The fixed standard height suits an average person, which is why sit-stand desks that adjust are popular.
How high these are off the floor.Kitchen counter: In the US it is 36 inches, a standard that matches dishwasher and range heights.
How high these are off the floor.Light switch: US codes usually place them near 48 inches, to be within easy reach.
How high these are off the floor.Top of a standard door: The standard US interior door is six feet eight inches tall.
How high these are off the floor.Ceiling: The eight-foot ceiling comes from standard 4-by-8-foot plywood and drywall sheets.
How high these are off the floor.Basketball hoop: Nailed to a gym balcony by James Naismith in 1891, it has stayed 10 feet high ever since.
How high these are off the floor.Two-storey house roof: Falls from roofs are a leading cause of construction deaths.
How high these are off the floor.Telephone pole: Typical poles are about 40 feet tall and buried roughly six feet in the ground.

Elevations of airports above sea level.Amsterdam Schiphol: It is below sea level, built on a former lake bed, and its name means 'ship hole'.
Elevations of airports above sea level.London Heathrow: It got its name from the village of Heath Row, which was cleared for the airfield.
Elevations of airports above sea level.Madrid–Barajas: Madrid is one of the highest capitals in Europe, at roughly 650 m.
Elevations of airports above sea level.Kathmandu Tribhuvan: It is surrounded by mountains, which makes landings there tricky.
Elevations of airports above sea level.Denver International: Its mile-high altitude means thin air, and it has one of the longest runways in the US.
Elevations of airports above sea level.Mexico City International: The city sits so high that planes need a longer takeoff roll in the thin air.
Elevations of airports above sea level.El Dorado, Bogotá: The name recalls the legend of a golden city, and it is among Latin America's busiest.
Elevations of airports above sea level.Lukla, Nepal: Its short sloping runway ends in a cliff, and it is the gateway to Everest.
Elevations of airports above sea level.El Alto, La Paz: It is the world's highest international airport, so planes land faster than usual.
Elevations of airports above sea level.Daocheng Yading, China: It ranks among the highest civilian airports in the world, high on the Tibetan plateau.

Pixar's Up, in story order.Young Carl meets Ellie: Up (2009) was Pixar's first 3D film and the first animated film to open the Cannes Film Festival.
Pixar's Up, in story order.Carl and Ellie marry: The wordless montage of their life together lasts only a few minutes and is famous for making audiences cry.
Pixar's Up, in story order.Ellie passes away: Michael Giacchino composed the score and won an Oscar for it.
Pixar's Up, in story order.Balloons lift the house: The film shows about 20,000 balloons lifting the house, though real life would need far more.
Pixar's Up, in story order.Russell is on the porch: Russell was partly modelled on Pixar animator Peter Sohn.
Pixar's Up, in story order.Landing in South America: Paradise Falls was inspired by Venezuela's tepuis, the flat-topped mountains near Angel Falls.
Pixar's Up, in story order.They find Kevin the bird: Kevin turns out to be female, a surprise when she lays eggs.
Pixar's Up, in story order.Dug the talking dog: Dug is a golden retriever, and dogs' sense of smell is thousands of times better than ours.
Pixar's Up, in story order.Charles Muntz's airship: Charles Muntz's airship is the Spirit of Adventure, a nod to explorers of the age.
Pixar's Up, in story order.Russell's badge ceremony: The Wilderness Explorers parody Scouts, and Carl gives Russell the grape soda cap as an honour badge.

Christmas songs, by when they appeared.Joy to the World: Words by Isaac Watts, adapted from Psalm 98, and music arranged by Lowell Mason from Handel; it's among the most-published Christmas hymns in North America.
Christmas songs, by when they appeared.Silent Night: First performed in Austria; legend says the church organ broke, so it was written for guitar.
Christmas songs, by when they appeared.Jingle Bells: Originally titled One Horse Open Sleigh, it was reportedly the first song broadcast from space.
Christmas songs, by when they appeared.Santa Claus Is Comin' to Town: Written by J. Fred Coots and Haven Gillespie, and first recorded by Eddie Cantor.
Christmas songs, by when they appeared.White Christmas: Irving Berlin's song was first sung by Bing Crosby in the film Holiday Inn.
Christmas songs, by when they appeared.Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer: Gene Autry's recording was a hit, from the Montgomery Ward story, and Johnny Marks wrote the song.
Christmas songs, by when they appeared.Jingle Bell Rock: Bobby Helms's song features a guitar riff by Hank Garland.
Christmas songs, by when they appeared.Last Christmas: George Michael played all the instruments for the Wham! song, which famously missed number one in 1984 but got there decades later.
Christmas songs, by when they appeared.Fairytale of New York: The Pogues' duet with Kirsty MacColl was held off the UK top spot by the Pet Shop Boys.
Christmas songs, by when they appeared.All I Want for Christmas: Mariah Carey co-wrote it, and it has returned to the top of the charts every December in recent years.
